relations: Dry branches and leaves fuel the fire, so flames flicker and shift as material burns away.
Hot gases rise, so smoke billows upward and drifts with ambient air currents over the grass.
Charred edges glow red, so embers brighten and fade as underlying fuel is consumed.
Surrounding green grass stays unburned unless flames spread, so it remains mostly intact near the pile.
